graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the base connection so the split reads as one street-building with an active ground threshold instead of two loose pieces.
Thicken the grounded base to improve mass continuity and give the lower edge more civic weight.
Open the split further to make the central seam legible as usable public space rather than a shallow separation.
Increase the puncture so the void contributes more visibly to public space and daylight logic.

rationale: The candidate is a compact two-block mass with a split-wing gesture and a puncture, so it is not incoherent, but it still reads primarily as adjacent rectangular solids rather than one strongly organized neighborhood building. Across the four views, the mass is coherent enough to understand, yet the dominant gesture is weakly expressed and the void is too minor to qualify as a clear public threshold. The blue access edge is acknowledged only indirectly; the form does not decisively open, bend, or carve toward it. Programmatically, neighborhood living wants an active ground edge, one legible public void/court/terrace, and calm upper massing; this candidate has the compact scale but not enough ground-legibility or section logic to hard-pass. The shape also skews toward a generic split block rather than a clearly lived-in street-building typology.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and curved than the candidate; do not copy the facade or roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a large central void and a bridge-like upper connector can create a clear public threshold for neighborhood-scale program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much smaller and more compact; avoid tower-like or overly dispersed composition.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a landscaped court shows how separate masses can still read as one civic ensemble.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has a clearer public cut and more confident ground-floor openness than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A simple rectangular mass can work when it is cut by a legible void and an overhang that activates the ground plane.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the same roof articulation and spatial continuity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise massing with a central atrium/courtyard and a folded roof can support neighborhood mixed-use identity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is less legible as a connected civic section and reads more like split blocks.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Multiple wings tied by bridges and terraces can preserve a shared public core while varying the upper massing.

warnings: Hard program-fit failed: the visible mass does not yet show a convincing active ground threshold or public void aligned to the access edge.
The silhouette is readable but still close to an arbitrary split-and-puncture box; step/cascade quality is not yet purposeful.
No obvious view-to-view collision problems, but the two wings remain visually under-bound and the void is underpowered.
